title: Read-only cross-PR record view (ODOC-330): propose lore's command shape and agree provenance/coverage fields with quest-cli
description: "Operator-chosen design, first-party in the opum-doc session (relayed to opum-agent as R-2026-09-29-21, filed here on the orchestrator's dispatch). Binding record read by ref at opum-doc 8b1c331: docs/adr/keep-lore-and-quest-records-on-the-branch-with-a-read-only-view-across-open-prs.md (opum-ai/opum-doc#557, ODOC-330, Accepted 2026-09-29). Records stay ATOMIC WITH THEIR CHANGE'S BRANCH; lore gains the same READ-ONLY view quest gets: origin/dev plus every open-PR head, per-record provenance (ref, owner/repo#N, the SHA read), coverage reported, conflicts shown and never merged. lore sync regenerates a branch's lore:tasks blocks ONLY from that branch; the view never writes. Ships in a pair release. THIS TASK IS THE PROPOSAL, NOT THE BUILD: propose lore's command shape for the ADR back through the orchestrator, and agree the provenance and coverage fields with quest-cli, which is doing the same on its side. Read the ADR by ref before proposing; do not implement until the orchestrator dispatches it."

acceptanceCriteria.text: The proposal (command surface, provenance fields, coverage reporting, and where the read-only view hooks into lore) is sent back through opum-agent for the operator's decision.
The provenance and coverage fields are agreed with quest-cli's proposal (both CLIs read the same records); any divergence is named rather than absorbed.

plan: 1. Read the ODOC-330 ADR by ref and lore's current carrier surface (query/read/manifest/envelope/git adapter) to fix where the view hooks in.
2. Measure the ref population first-party in lore-cli (historical refs/pull/*/head vs open PRs into dev) to reproduce quest-cli's settling measurement.

3. Draft the command shape: carrier command, flag surface, per-record provenance key and fields, coverage reporting, exit codes, and the hook-point modules. Name every divergence from quest-cli's agreed shape rather than absorbing it.
4. Record the proposal on this task and send it to opum-agent; do not implement.
implementationNotes: FIELD AGREEMENT WITH QUEST-CLI, recorded for the proposal (their side: QCLI-417, filed as opum-ai/quest-cli#436; they relay both the agreement and the measurements to opum-agent). Agreed verbatim: flag `--across-refs`; per-record provenance {ref, pullRequest, sha} (full 40-hex, pullRequest null when no PR); top-level coverage {complete, population, discoveredAt, refsRead[], refsUnreadable[]}; envelope placement after data, before principal; exits 0 complete / 6 incomplete naming the unreadable refs / 3 when origin or origin/dev is absent / never 5 for content conflicts; `--allow-partial` downgrades 6 to 0 with complete:false; conflicts are data. THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLED THE ENUM (quest-cli, 2026-09-29): `git ls-remote origin 'refs/pull/*/head'` returns 435 refs on their repo while `gh pr list --state open` returns 0 -- the PR ref namespace is HISTORICAL and carries no base, so a git-only mechanism can never back population:'open-prs' or complete:true. Settlement: population stays {open-prs, explicit, dev-only}; open-prs REQUIRES a forge-aware, base-filtered discovery and NOTHING git-only may set it; explicit covers git-only reads of NAMED refs, with complete relative to the named set; complete is ALWAYS relative to the population named in the same object. QUEST-CLI'S PRODUCTION PIN (accepted): on quest, dev-only is only ever a DEGRADED outcome -- it appears when --across-refs was requested, discovery was unavailable, and the caller passed --allow-partial; without --allow-partial that state exits 6, and quest never emits dev-only with complete:true, because a request that was repository-wide cannot be answered by naming a narrower population as if it were the answer. STILL OPEN FOR THIS TASK'S PROPOSAL, to be stated as scope decisions rather than defaults: which lore command carries the view (query or read); whether lore's no-flags default is forge-aware (a NEW dependency -- lore has none today) or git-only, and if the latter, say plainly that a git-only default cannot answer the ADR's open-PR semantic. Propose, do not implement; ships in a pair release.

PROPOSAL for LCLI-651 / ODOC-330 — lore's read-only cross-ref record view. Sent to opum-agent 2026-09-29; NOT implemented. Read the ADR by ref before acting on this: opum-doc 8b1c331, docs/adr/keep-lore-and-quest-records-on-the-branch-with-a-read-only-view-across-open-prs.md (Accepted 2026-09-29).

SURFACES READ (at origin/dev fdce743e, this session): commands/query.ts, commands/read.ts, commands/args.ts, core/retrieval.ts, core/query.ts (QueryHit), core/workspace-retrieval.ts, core/workspace-contract.ts, core/workspace-source.ts, core/manifest.ts (query entry), output.ts (SuccessEnvelope/emit), adapters/git.ts, errors.ts (EXIT_CODES).

MEASURED IN THIS REPO, first-party, 2026-09-29 — reproduces quest-cli's settling measurement in their repo:
- `git ls-remote origin 'refs/pull/*/head' | wc -l` -> 424
- `gh pr list --state open --json number | jq length` -> 0; `--base dev` -> 0
- `git for-each-ref refs/pull | wc -l` -> 0 — NO PR object is local; a discovered PR head must be fetched before its tree can be read
- `gh pr list --state all --json number,headRefName,headRefOid,baseRefName` works here (field set proven live, not assumed)
So in lore-cli too, a git-only mechanism cannot back population=open-prs: 424 historical refs, 0 open, none local.

1. CARRIER: `lore query`. The ADR's own context sentence names it ("a document added on an open PR is invisible to `lore query` until it merges"), and query is the listing surface whose answers become repository-true. `lore read` is not carried in this release (decision D4).

2. FLAGS (declared only on `query` in core/manifest.ts; parsed like `workspaceSelection` in commands/args.ts):
- `--across-refs` (bare): population `open-prs` — origin/dev plus every open PR into dev.
- `--across-refs <ref>` (repeatable): population `explicit`; each value a ref name resolved locally. Mixing bare and valued occurrences is a usage error (2); so is `--allow-partial` without `--across-refs`, and `--across-refs` together with `--workspace`/`--repository` (one explicit scope per invocation).
- `--allow-partial`: downgrades 6 to 0 with `coverage.complete:false`.
- Registered on read-only commands only. `sync` never (ADR 6: sync regenerates a branch's `<!-- lore:tasks -->` blocks only from that branch's own records). check/link/replace honestly unchanged.
- The view never reads the working tree — a branch's committed tip is the observation. Uncommitted local edits are what plain `lore query` is for.

3. PER-RECORD PROVENANCE: `hit.refProvenance` = {ref, pullRequest, sha}, inner shape verbatim as agreed — `ref` the exact ref read (`refs/heads/dev`, `refs/pull/437/head`); `pullRequest` `owner/repo#N`, null for origin/dev; `sha` the full 40-hex commit read, never abbreviated.
NAMED DIVERGENCE #1 (for a ruling, not absorbed): the agreed field name `provenance` is already taken on this exact payload. `query.results` hits carry `provenance` today in `--workspace` mode holding a `WorkspaceRecordProvenance` (repository identity/digest keys; core/query.ts:182). A second, unrelated shape on the same key makes the key's meaning depend on which flags ran, and both wrong readings are silent: `hit.provenance.ref` is undefined in workspace mode, `hit.provenance.memberId` is undefined in cross-ref mode. Proposal A (recommended): lore names it `refProvenance`; quest keeps `provenance`; the inner object is byte-identical so one reader serves both. Proposal B: key parity at `provenance`, which requires a breaking change to lore's shipped `query.results` kind (relocate workspace provenance, bump per cli-contract §7.1).

4. COVERAGE: top-level envelope key, after `data`, before `principal`, exactly as agreed: {complete, population, discoveredAt, refsRead[], refsUnreadable[]}. lore's envelope is built in one place (output.ts `successEnvelope`) and validated post-serialization, so this is an optional envelope extension on `Renderable`/`successEnvelope`; additive under cli-contract §7, no schemaVersion bump. Fact, not objection: lore's existing scope-ish payloads sit inside `data` today (`data.workspace`, `data.backend`), so top-level is a new convention for lore — it is the agreed one and lore will match it. `complete` is always relative to the population named in the same object (quest-cli's pin, adopted verbatim).

5. ROWS AND CONFLICTS (ADR 4/5 — shown, never merged, no winner): rows are (id, ref) observations. An id present on origin/dev always emits dev's row; another ref's copy of that id emits a row only when its file bytes differ from dev's. An id not on dev emits one row per ref that carries it. Divergent copies therefore appear as several rows with the same id: the conflict IS the data, no extra field, nothing merged. Equality is the concept file's bytes at its bundle path, computed by lore (not a git OID), so it survives the materialization path in §8.

6. EXITS: 0 complete; 6 incomplete, naming `refsUnreadable` — including when discovery itself is unavailable (no forge) and `--allow-partial` was not passed; 3 when `origin` or `origin/dev` is absent; never 5 for content conflicts (5 stays quest's write-conflict semantic). `--allow-partial` downgrades 6 to 0 with complete:false. dev-only is only ever a degraded outcome, adopted verbatim from quest-cli's accepted pin: it appears when `--across-refs` was requested, discovery was unavailable, and `--allow-partial` was passed; lore never emits dev-only with complete:true. query's manifest exitCodes widen from ["bundle"] to include git.

7. WHERE IT HOOKS IN (existing seams):
- `src/adapters/forge.ts` (new): injectable `ForgeAdapter`, `listOpenPullRequests({base}) -> {number, headRefName, headRefOid}[]`; default impl shells `gh pr list --state open --base dev --json number,headRefName,headRefOid`. Mirrors adapters/backlog.ts + adapters/git.ts (real adapter behind an injectable seam). lore handles no credentials.
- `src/core/cross-ref.ts` (new): ref resolution -> object availability -> per-ref bundle load -> merge -> coverage. Per-ref load uses the reference loader (loadBundle) only: no Ladybug/indexed involvement and no `.lore/cache` writes for other refs.
- `src/commands/query.ts`: a third loader branch beside `--workspace` and the plain path; `finishQuery` stamps `refProvenance` from a `CrossRefRetrievalContext` exactly as it stamps workspace provenance today.
- `src/core/retrieval.ts`: `RetrievalGraph` gains optional `crossRef?:` (mirrors `workspace?:`).
- `src/commands/args.ts`: `acrossRefsSelection(parsed)` mirroring `workspaceSelection`.
- `src/core/manifest.ts`: the flags on query only, plus widened exit codes.
- `output.ts`: the optional envelope extension for coverage.
- `src/core/query.ts`: QueryHit gains `refProvenance?`; the pure engine is otherwise untouched.

8. READING ANOTHER REF — mechanism and the one write it implies: discovered PR heads are not local (0 local refs/pull/* measured), so the view fetches each discovered ref before reading its tree: `git fetch --no-tags origin <ref>` (objects + FETCH_HEAD only; no branch or remote-tracking ref is moved), then materializes the bundle with `git archive <sha> docs | tar -x -C <per-run temp dir>` and loads it with the existing filesystem loader. The working tree and the index are never touched, and the ADR's "the view never writes" governs branch files — naming this here rather than smuggling it. Explicit population does not fetch: those refs must already resolve locally (that is the git-only/offline path). A ref that cannot be fetched or resolved is `refsUnreadable`, not a fatal error.
Deferred alternative, named not chosen: `git ls-tree -r` + `git cat-file --batch` streaming behind a bundle-source seam — no temp files, but loadBundle is filesystem-based (readdirSync/readFileSync) and would need a source abstraction; not v1.

9. TEXT RENDERING: pretty/plain print a coverage footer line when the view ran (e.g. `coverage: origin/dev + 3 open PRs (4 refs read, 0 unreadable)`; incomplete reads name the unreadable refs). This is the human half of ADR 7's positive control — an empty listing that says "nothing documented" must carry how much was read in the same output. JSON placement unaffected. `--limit` keeps its meaning (caps rows; existing truncation footer).

DECISIONS FOR THE OPERATOR (A/B, recommendation first):
D1 forge mechanism — needs a ruling AND must match quest-cli's. A (recommended) `gh` shell-out behind an injectable seam: no credentials in lore, authenticated by the user's own gh, and it reproduces the discovery quest-cli already measured with. B: GitHub REST via fetch with a token lore reads from the environment — no external CLI, but lore then owns auth, token precedence, and its own network stack. (C, explicit-refs-only with no open-prs population, cannot answer the ADR and is listed only to be rejected.)
D2 per-record key — named divergence #1 above. A (recommended) `refProvenance`, inner shape identical. B unified `provenance` with a breaking `query.results` bump.
D3 fetch — A (recommended) fetch discovered refs as in §8. B never fetch: on a fresh checkout every PR head is unreadable (0 local refs measured), so the view answers nothing — it cannot answer the ADR.
D4 `lore read` — A (recommended) not carried in this release: read returns ONE body, and a discovery-based read has no honest answer when copies differ (ADR 5 forbids picking winners). B carry it for the explicit population only (`lore read <id> --across-refs <ref>`), never discovery, as a later increment.
D5 scores with more than one ref — BM25 scores are per-ref and not comparable across refs. A (recommended) keep the ref-local score, order dev first then PRs ascending, and document the number as ref-local. B omit `score` whenever more than one ref is in scope.
D6 no ref cap in v1 — a silent cap is what coverage forbids, and the agreed coverage shape has no "discovered but not attempted" list. A (recommended) no cap; the pair release's qualification measures the N-ref cost (loadBundle's boundedMemory lever exists if needed). B add a cap now, which needs a new coverage field and therefore a new agreement.

OPEN, NOT MINE TO SETTLE: whether quest's `scope`/`unseenTaskIds` pairing has a lore analogue worth building on (lore has no scope/unseen concept today); and that lore-cli itself has 0 open PRs, so the view's real cost is unmeasurable here and wants a many-PR repo at qualification.

NOT IMPLEMENTED, as instructed. Implementation waits on the orchestrator's dispatch.
finalSummary:
Proposed lore's command shape for ODOC-330's read-only cross-ref view and sent it through opum-agent on 2026-09-29 (cross-session message, msg_id 3e260f65); no implementation, as instructed. The proposal is note 2 on this record: `lore query` carries the view; flags `--across-refs[=<ref>]` and `--allow-partial`; per-hit `refProvenance {ref, pullRequest, sha}` (inner shape verbatim as agreed with quest-cli) with top-level `coverage {complete, population, discoveredAt, refsRead[], refsUnreadable[]}` placed after data and before principal; exits 0 complete / 6 incomplete naming the unreadable refs / 3 when origin or origin/dev is absent / never 5 for content conflicts; dev-only only as a degraded outcome, never complete:true; hook points named at existing seams (adapters/forge.ts, core/cross-ref.ts, commands/query.ts, core/retrieval.ts, commands/args.ts, core/manifest.ts, output.ts, core/query.ts). Verified rather than asserted: the ADR read by ref at opum-doc 8b1c331; lore's surface read at origin/dev fdce743e; the ref population measured first-party in this repo (424 historical refs/pull/*/head, 0 open PRs, 0 local PR refs, and the `gh pr list --json` field set proven live). Two divergences from quest-cli's agreed shape are named in the proposal rather than absorbed — the per-hit key is `refProvenance` because `provenance` is already a shipped workspace field on `query.results` (core/query.ts:182), and top-level coverage is a new convention for lore (its scope-ish payloads sit inside `data` today) — and both are routed to the operator, along with the forge mechanism, the fetch question, the `lore read` scope, per-ref BM25 scores, and the no-cap decision, as the A/B set D1-D6. The build is unstarted: it waits on the orchestrator's dispatch after the operator's ruling.

Landed as opum-ai/lore-cli#426, which is this record's completion, both checked criteria and this summary as its only content. The run that validated the deliverable is 36567917983 on 13c94f98 — twelve contexts success plus one skipped (`promotion is manual`, skipped by design on every dev pull request), with all six contexts dev's ruleset requires green: docker e2e harness (real lore + backlog binaries), Tracker integrity, lint · typecheck · test on ubuntu-latest and on windows-latest, lore check (docs gate), and compile smoke (ubuntu). The tracker-only citation commit that follows is covered by the merge gate on the pull request's own final head, not by that run.
